study.title: Brain regions involved in moxibustion-induced analgesia in irritable bowel syndrome with diarrhea: a functional magnetic resonance imaging study
study.article_type: randomized controlled trial with neuroimaging substudy
study.study_design: Randomized controlled trial; eighty D-IBS patients randomly divided into moxibustion and sham moxibustion group for a 4-week treatment; subset underwent fMRI during rectal balloon distention before and after treatment
study.randomization: Computer-generated randomization sequence; sequence concealed through sealed, opaque, sequentially numbered envelopes
study.blinding: Patients were blinded to group assignment
study.population: Right-handed patients with diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome (D-IBS) recruited from outpatient clinic of Shanghai Research Institute of Acupuncture and Meridian and Shanghai Community Health Service Center of Shi Men Er Road, April 2010 to November 2011
study.disease_condition: Diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome (D-IBS), diagnosed per Rome III criteria
study.inclusion_criteria: Each patient met the Rome III criteria of D-IBS; right-handed
study.exclusion_criteria: Clinically relevant gastrointestinal, hepatic, or other systemic diseases; bowel resections or abdominal operations; any medication administered in preceding 30 days; pregnancy or lactation; epilepsy

neuroimaging_methods.scanner_manufacturer_model_exact: 1.5 T GE Scanner (Exicte HD, General Electric Medical System, Milwaukee, WI, USA) with an 8-channel NVHEAD coil
neuroimaging_methods.sequence_exact: blood-oxygen-level-dependent (BOLD) protocol with a T2*-weighted gradient echo-planar imaging (EPI) sequence; anatomical: high-resolution T1-weighted anatomical protocol
neuroimaging_methods.voxel_size_exact: resliced to isotropic 2 mm 3 voxels; slice thickness 5 mm (functional); slice thickness 1.4 mm (anatomical)
neuroimaging_methods.scan_duration_exact: 60 whole brain volume acquisitions, divided into three cycles; total 180 s per run; extra baseline (12 s) added at beginning
neuroimaging_methods.analysis_software_exact: statistical parametric mapping 2 (SPM2) (Wellcome Department of Cognitive Neurology, London, UK; http://www.fil.ion.ucl.ac.uk/spm/software/spm2/)
neuroimaging_methods.smoothing_exact: 5 mm (full width half maximum) Gaussian filter applied to each image
neuroimaging_methods.motion_exclusion_exact: correction for acceptable head movement between the images in each session was performed by alignment with one image; head immobilized with padded earmuffs and foam headrest; subjects instructed to refrain from movement as much as possible
statistical_thresholds_exact: alpha level of P ≤ 0.05 (uncorrected for multiple comparisons)
neuroimaging_methods.multiple_comparison_correction_exact: continuous random field theory, assuming the statistic image to be a good lattice representation of an underlying continuous stationary random field; inference based on corrected p-values
neuroimaging_methods.source_location: Methods/Brain fMRI scans/Imaging procedure and Data analysis sections, pages 4-5

extraction_notes.note: Table 3 reports control group IBS QOL Scale after-treatment value as 73.62 ± 7.42, but the Results text on page 7 states 'from 80.54 ± 8.27 to 70.62 ± 7.42.' These two values differ (73.62 vs 70.62). The table value (73.62) was extracted as primary, with the text value noted.
Expectancy, credibility, and blinding success were not assessed or reported. The paper states patients were blinded to group assignment but provides no formal measure of blinding success.
Deqi sensations were not reported or assessed for moxibustion or sham moxibustion procedures.

Coordinate space is not explicitly stated in the results tables. The methods state normalization to Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) space, so MNI is inferred for all reported coordinates. No explicit label appears in Tables 5 or 6.
extraction_notes.source_location: Methods/Data analysis section page 5; Tables 5 and 6 page 8

extraction_notes.note: The neuroimaging substudy sample sizes (n=15 moxibustion, n=13 control) differ from the main clinical trial sample sizes (n=40 per arm). Clinical outcomes in Tables 2 and 3 are labeled with the neuroimaging substudy sample sizes (n=15, n=13) in the table, not the full trial sample. It is unclear whether Tables 2 and 3 refer to the full trial sample or only the fMRI substudy participants.
extraction_notes.source_location: Tables 2 and 3 page 5; Methods/Participants section pages 2-3

extraction_notes.note: The p-values reported in Table 6 for moxibustion group after-treatment ACC coordinate (4, -52, 24) is 0.991, which appears to be not significant at the stated threshold of P ≤ 0.05 (uncorrected). Similarly, the PFC coordinate (6, 60, -6) has p = 0.993. These high p-values after corrections are counterintuitive and may reflect corrected p-values differing from uncorrected. Extracted as reported.

The paper states both uncorrected (P ≤ 0.05) and corrected (continuous random field theory) p-values are used, but does not clarify which p-values appear in the tables. Both types are referenced in the statistical methods. Some table p-values exceed 0.05 (e.g., 0.993, 0.997, 0.991) suggesting these may be corrected cluster-level p-values.
extraction_notes.source_location: Methods/Data analysis section page 5-7; Tables 5 and 6 page 8

extraction_notes.note: The Brodmann area (BA) column in Tables 5 and 6 contains dashes (----) for some rows, indicating the Brodmann area was not identified for those peaks. These are extracted as 'not_reported'.

Units for rectal distention threshold values (first sensation, defecation urge, pain detection) are not explicitly stated in Table 4. Based on context (rectal balloon distention with air in ml), these are inferred to be ml.

Table 4 reports the difference for 'defecation urge threshold' in control group as 2.85 ± 1.68 [95% CI: -0.80, 6.50], consistent with non-significant change. The 95% CI crosses zero, supporting the reported non-significance. Extracted as reported.

The paper does not report the number of sessions as a single integer. The treatment is described as 'three times per week for two weeks as a course of treatment; every patient had two courses.' This implies approximately 12 sessions total over 4 weeks, but this is not stated explicitly.
The flip angle for the functional EPI sequence is reported as 90 degrees. FOV for the functional sequence is not explicitly stated (only given for anatomical: 24 cm × 18 cm).

The paper describes activation results for 50 ml distention in the moxibustion group after treatment as 'the prefrontal cortex (PFC) was affected' and in the control group as 'the PFC and the anterior cingulated cortex (ACC) were affected.' The word 'affected' is used in the abstract but 'activated' is used in the results section and tables. These appear to refer to the same findings.
extraction_notes.source_location: Abstract page 1; Results/Brain fMRI section page 8

extraction_notes.note: Data on activation in other brain areas during rectal balloon distention (temporal lobe, primary visual cortex, cerebellum) are mentioned in the Discussion but not reported in tables, as the authors state there was no difference between groups in these areas.

The Table 4 footnote symbols (▲, ★, ●, ○) are used to indicate statistical comparisons. ▲ p = 0.000 compared with baseline and control group for defecation urge threshold after moxibustion; ★ p = 0.000 for the difference; ● p = 0.001 compared with baseline for pain detection threshold; ○ p = 0.005 for the difference between groups. These have been integrated into the respective sensory response entries.
